report_name: SickKids Hospital Discloses Employee Data Breach from Third-Party App

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The data breach was caused by a security vulnerability within an unnamed third-party software application used by SickKids, allowing unauthorized actors to access systems containing employee and applicant data. This represents a compromise of a downstream customer via a vendor's product.

identities.name: The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids)
identities.description: A hospital in Toronto, Canada, that suffered a data breach impacting employee and applicant personal information due to a vulnerability in a third-party application.

identities.name: Boomerang Health
identities.description: A clinic affiliated with SickKids whose employees may also have been impacted by the data breach.

identities.name: SickKids Foundation
identities.description: A foundation affiliated with SickKids whose employees may also have been impacted by the data breach.

indicators.name: Potential Web Shell Command Execution via Third-Party App
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Web Shell Command Execution via Third-Party App
id: 2b9c1a8e-4f5d-4b6c-8a1b-9e0d3c2a1b3e
status: experimental
description: Detects a command shell process spawning from a common web server process, which could indicate post-exploitation activity following a web application compromise.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-24
references:
  - https://www.sickkids.ca/en/news/archive/2026/SickKids-employee-information-impacted-by-cybersecurity-incident/
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\tomcat.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects command shells spawning from web server processes, a common TTP for attackers after exploiting a web application vulnerability to gain execution.

indicators.name: Potential Web Shell File Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Web Shell File Creation
id: f8d7e6c5-4b3a-4c2d-8e1f-0a9b8c7d6e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of files with common web shell extensions in web server directories. This can indicate an attacker dropping a web shell for persistence after exploiting a vulnerability.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-24
references:
  - https://www.sickkids.ca/en/news/archive/2026/SickKids-employee-information-impacted-by-cybersecurity-incident/
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.aspx'
      - '.asp'
      - '.php'
      - '.jsp'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\wwwroot\'
      - '\inetpub\'
      - '\public_html\'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of potential web shell files in web root directories, a common attacker technique for maintaining persistence after exploiting a web application.
